activities.context: You look at the sky. A rainbow is there. It is very big, and it is full of light. The rainbow goes across the sky. The sky has no clouds. The sky is blue. The rainbow stretches over that blue sky with no clouds. A very big rainbow is there, and a bright rainbow is there.
activities.prompt: If someone asks what the sky is like in the case, what should you tell them?
options: It is cloudless and not blue.
It is cloudy and not blue.

Wrong: the case says the sky has no clouds, not clouds.
Wrong: the case says the sky is blue, not that it has no blue colour.
Wrong: this changes both facts: it adds clouds and takes away the blue colour.

activities.explanation: Correct: the case says there are no clouds and the sky is blue.

activities.context: You look at the sky. A rainbow is there. It is very big, and it is full of light. The rainbow goes across the sky. The sky has no clouds. The sky is blue. The rainbow stretches over that blue sky with no clouds. A very big rainbow is there, and a bright rainbow is there.
activities.prompt: The rainbow is very big. What would you say to show that it goes across the sky?
options: It reaches from one part of the sky to another.
It stays in one part of the sky.
It stays under the blue sky.
It stays behind the blue sky.

Wrong: staying in one part does not show it goes across the sky.
Wrong: staying under the sky does not show it goes across the sky.
Wrong: staying behind the sky does not show it goes across the sky.

activities.explanation: Correct: going across the sky means it reaches over the sky.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between the sky and the rainbow in the lesson?
activities.answer: The sky has no clouds and is blue. The rainbow is very big and full of light. The rainbow goes across the sky and stretches over the clear blue sky.
points: sky has no clouds
sky is blue
rainbow is very big and full of light
rainbow goes across and stretches over the sky
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: One day, Anandi ran outside to her garden. Milli ran along with her and stayed beside her. Milli was Anandi's pet cat, the cat Anandi liked best. Anandi liked to make drawings and put colour on pictures. That day, Anandi wished to paint the flowers in her garden using rainbow colours.
activities.prompt: Anandi begins to paint the flowers she wished to make colourful. What will she most likely use?
options: Colours of the rainbow on the flowers.
Only one plain colour on the flowers.
Colours of the rainbow on Milli.
No colour at all on the picture.

Her wish was for rainbow colours, not one plain colour.
She wished to paint flowers, not Milli.
She liked to put colour on pictures, so no colour would not fit.

activities.explanation: She wished to use rainbow colours for her flower painting.

activities.context: One day, Anandi ran outside to her garden. Milli ran along with her and stayed beside her. Milli was Anandi's pet cat, the cat Anandi liked best. Anandi liked to make drawings and put colour on pictures. That day, Anandi wished to paint the flowers in her garden using rainbow colours.
activities.prompt: Anandi has made a picture of the flowers in her garden. What would show that she used her wish?
options: The flowers have colours of the rainbow.

She wished to put the colours on her flower picture, not on Milli.
She liked to put colour on pictures, so a colourless picture would not show her wish.
She wished to paint flowers, so the picture would show flowers.

activities.explanation: She wished to use rainbow colours for painting the garden flowers.

activities.prompt: How does the fact that Milli was beside Anandi help us know where Milli was when Anandi ran to her garden?
activities.answer: Milli ran along with Anandi and was beside her. Anandi ran outside to her garden. So when Anandi got there, Milli was with her, close beside her. Milli was Anandi's pet cat.
points: Milli ran along with Anandi.
Milli was beside Anandi.
Anandi ran outside to her garden.
So Milli was with Anandi near the garden.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Anandi puts colours on flowers. She uses violet for one flower and indigo for another flower. Indigo is one of the rainbow colours. She uses blue for one flower. She uses green for the leaves. She uses orange for one flower. She uses red for one flower. She does not use yellow for a flower. She saves yellow for the Sun. The Sun could look bright and cheerful.
activities.prompt: Anandi is putting colours on flowers. She comes to a flower and wants to keep yellow for the Sun. What should she do?
options: Use one of the colours she already put on other flowers.
Use yellow for this flower and for the Sun.
Use green for this flower because leaves are green.
Use no colour for this flower because yellow is saved.

why.Use yellow for this flower and for the S: Wrong: using yellow on a flower would not keep yellow for the Sun.
why.Use green for this flower because leaves: Wrong: green was used for the leaves, not as the colour to use while saving yellow.
why.Use no colour for this flower because ye: Wrong: she puts colours on flowers, so the flower can still get a colour.

activities.explanation: Right: yellow is kept for the Sun, so a flower colour she already used can be chosen.

activities.context: Anandi puts colours on flowers. She uses violet for one flower and indigo for another flower. Indigo is one of the rainbow colours. She uses blue for one flower. She uses green for the leaves. She uses orange for one flower. She uses red for one flower. She does not use yellow for a flower. She saves yellow for the Sun. The Sun could look bright and cheerful.
activities.prompt: Anandi decides to put yellow on a flower. What would be different?
options: Yellow would go on a flower, not stay saved for the Sun.
Yellow would go on the Sun, not stay saved for a flower.
Green would go on the Sun, not stay on the leaves.
Indigo would go on the leaves, not stay on a flower.

why.Yellow would go on the Sun, not stay sav: Wrong: yellow was saved for the Sun, not for a flower.
why.Green would go on the Sun, not stay on t: Wrong: green was used for the leaves.
why.Indigo would go on the leaves, not stay: Wrong: indigo was used for another flower.

activities.explanation: Right: putting yellow on a flower changes the plan to save it for the Sun.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between how Anandi used green and how she used yellow?
activities.answer: Anandi used green for the leaves. She did not use yellow for a flower; she saved yellow for the Sun. So green went on the leaves, while yellow was kept for the Sun, which could look bright and cheerful.
points: Green was used for the leaves.
Yellow was not used for a flower.
Yellow was saved for the Sun.
The Sun could look bright and cheerful.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Lovely flowers cover the garden. The flowers are spread all over the garden. The Sun is up in the sky and gives light. The Sun shines with yellow beauty and has a yellow shine. The rainbow has disappeared after colouring the flowers and the Sun. The flowers look lovely.
activities.prompt: The rainbow is not in the sky now. What did it do before it went?
options: It put colour on the flowers and the Sun.
It took the yellow shine from the Sun.
It made the flowers cover the whole sky.
It stopped the Sun from giving light.

Wrong: the Sun had a yellow shine.
Wrong: the flowers covered and spread over the garden.
Wrong: the Sun was up and giving light.

activities.explanation: Right: it coloured the flowers and the Sun before disappearing.

activities.context: Lovely flowers cover the garden. The flowers are spread all over the garden. The Sun is up in the sky and gives light. The Sun shines with yellow beauty and has a yellow shine. The rainbow has disappeared after colouring the flowers and the Sun. The flowers look lovely.
activities.prompt: Look at the lovely flowers. Which reason best explains why they look lovely?
options: The rainbow had coloured them before it disappeared.
The Sun had spread them all over the garden.
The flowers had coloured the rainbow.
The Sun had disappeared after giving light.

why.The Sun had spread them all over the gar: Wrong: flowers were spread all over the garden, not by the Sun.
Wrong: the rainbow coloured the flowers, not the other way round.
why.The Sun had disappeared after giving lig: Wrong: the Sun was giving light; it had not disappeared.

activities.explanation: Right: the rainbow coloured the flowers before it went away.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between what the rainbow did and what the Sun did in the case?
activities.answer: The rainbow coloured the flowers and the Sun before it disappeared. The Sun was up in the sky, gave light, shone with yellow beauty, and had a yellow shine. So the rainbow disappeared, but the Sun gave light and had a yellow shine.
points: Rainbow coloured the flowers.
Rainbow coloured the Sun and then disappeared.
Sun was up in the sky and gave light.
Sun shone with yellow beauty and had a yellow shine.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.
